## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The reset and signup validators now correctly require 12 characters, and their tests cover the new boundary. The invite validator, which has the same structure, was not updated, so the new minimum is not enforced everywhere. The PR body says the change "raises the minimum in the password validators".

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/signup.py:1 — correctness — This PR raises `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` to 12 in `app/signup.py` and `app/reset.py`, but the stale `app/invite.py:1` still has `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8`. As a result, `app.invite.accepts_password("abcdefghi")` (9 characters) still returns `True`, and `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` still checks the old `length >= 8` boundary. Could you raise `app/invite.py:1` to 12 and update `tests/test_invite.py` to the `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` boundaries used in the other two tests? Alternatively, all three modules could import one shared constant. — Passwords of 8–11 characters set through the invite flow still pass, which breaks the 12-character security policy this PR is meant to enforce.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_reset.py:6` and `tests/test_signup.py:6` test lengths 11, 12, and 13, so an off-by-one error at the new minimum would fail the tests. They also keep 8 as a case that was accepted before and must now be rejected.
